name: Netdata
what_it_is: Netdata is an open-source, real-time infrastructure monitoring platform that collects per-second metrics from systems, containers, applications, and hardware with zero configuration. It runs an edge-based observability pipeline including ML-powered anomaly detection, tiered time-series storage, alerting, and a built-in web dashboard accessible on port 19999.
components: Netdata Agent — core monitoring engine handling collection, storage, ML, alerts, streaming, and API
go.d.plugin — Go-based data collector covering 800+ integrations (nginx, postgres, redis, docker, etc.)
apps.plugin — per-process and per-user resource usage tracking
cgroups.plugin — Docker/LXC/Kubernetes container monitoring and cgroup metrics
proc.plugin — host kernel and network stack metrics via /proc
systemd-journal.plugin — systemd journal log viewing and analysis
network-viewer.plugin — live network socket map per PID
ML anomaly detection engine — per-metric unsupervised models trained at the edge
Netdata UI — closed-source dashboard served via CDN, accessible at http://NODE:19999
Netdata Cloud — optional SaaS layer for remote access, RBAC, and multi-node views (free tier available)
protocols: HTTP/HTTPS — REST API on port 19999 for metrics queries and dashboard
SNMP — network device monitoring via go.d.plugin SNMP collector
StatsD — custom application metrics ingestion on UDP 8125
OpenMetrics/Prometheus exposition format — scrape and expose endpoints
Netdata streaming protocol — Parent-Child real-time metric replication over TCP
measurement: Per-second metric collection (1-second resolution at Tier 0)
~0.5 bytes per sample storage efficiency with ZSTD compression
Anomaly Rate (AR) score per metric — toggle in dashboard
Metrics scoring engine for cross-metric pattern correlation
Disk flush interval: every 17 minutes, spread evenly to minimize I/O
configuration: Configuration files live in /etc/netdata inside the container (mapped to netdataconfig volume)
Environment variable NETDATA_CLAIM_TOKEN — token to connect node to Netdata Cloud
Environment variable NETDATA_CLAIM_URL — Netdata Cloud URL for node registration
Environment variable NETDATA_CLAIM_ROOMS — comma-separated room IDs for node placement
Disable telemetry: create /etc/netdata/.opt-out-from-anonymous-statistics or pass --disable-telemetry at install
Storage mode settable to alloc or ram for no-disk-write operation
fault_injection: No built-in fault injection mechanism; Netdata is a passive observer, not a chaos tool
Alert rules can be customized to fire on synthetic thresholds to test notification pipelines
Streaming can be interrupted to test Parent-Child failover behavior
modes: Standalone — single Agent with local dashboard and storage
Parent mode — centralized Agent receiving streams from Child Agents
Child mode — Agent streaming all metrics to a Parent, with optional local retention
alloc/ram storage mode — metrics held in memory only, no disk writes
Cloud-connected — Agent registered to Netdata Cloud for remote access and multi-node views
Kubernetes mode — deployed via Helm chart with per-node DaemonSet and parent Deployment
constraints: Requires host PID namespace (pid: host) and host network mode for full monitoring capabilities; missing these disables container network interface mapping and host networking metrics
Requires SYS_PTRACE and SYS_ADMIN capabilities and apparmor:unconfined security option; without them local-listeners and cgroups container name resolution are unavailable
Must mount /proc, /sys, /var/run/docker.sock, /run/dbus, /etc/passwd, /etc/group, /var/log, /etc/os-release from host for complete visibility; partial mounts yield partial metrics
Does not officially support --user or user: Compose parameter; some features may break when running as non-root from the start
Netdata Cloud is optional but required for remote access, SSO, RBAC, and centralized alert configuration; local dashboard only works on the same network without it
docker_services: netdata — single service using image netdata/netdata; exposes no ports explicitly because it uses network_mode: host (dashboard reachable at host:19999)
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml in the repository root; the canonical compose example is documented in packaging/docker/README.md only
No built-in log aggregation backend (relies on systemd-journald or external exporters)
No native OpenTelemetry ingestion yet (listed as coming soon)
No fault injection or synthetic load generation capabilities
No bundled alertmanager; notifications are pushed directly via Netdata's own notification integrations (Slack, PagerDuty, email, etc.)
